title: How deep is the stack?
description:
Watch the stack grow during recursion.

```
depth 0 at 0x7ffd...a0
depth 1 at 0x7ffd...50  (80 bytes per call)
depth 2 at 0x7ffd...00  (80 bytes per call)
with a 1 KB local array: 1056 bytes per call
```
hints: The stack usually grows downwards, so `previous - current` is the size of one frame (lesson 4.02).
The compiler may make the frame bigger than your locals for alignment and saved registers; the numbers depend on the build.
requirements: A recursive function prints the address of one of its locals at each depth, and the distance from the previous one.
Compare a function with no big locals and one with a `char buffer[1024]`.
Keep the recursion depth small (10) so it never overflows.
stretch: Build with `-O2` and see whether the compiler turns the recursion into a loop.
